verdict.rationale: Viam's own docs cover each step of bring-up. Drivers come from the Registry: you name the hardware model in config and viam-server pulls and initializes the driver. A first-machine wizard and a discovery service that suggests component configurations handle setup. Web test panels let you drive bases and move arms without deploying code, and a 'control a motor in 2 minutes' tutorial shows first motion (cloud simulation is available if hardware isn't). Community comments note the platform needs Linux-class compute with internet access, which limits the hardware it suits but doesn't contradict the bring-up claims. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the hours-not-weeks timeline; evidence on bring-up effort when no Registry driver exists and you must write a driver module; coverage of hardware without a high-level OS or network connectivity.
